reuse.why: Several consumers share the new helper, but it duplicates getScheduledAmount and getApproxNumberThreshold while the API implements its own resolution.

duplication.why: Amount dispatch, approximate tolerance calculation, and API expected-amount resolution duplicate logic available elsewhere in the tree or diff.

placement.why: Shared schedule logic belongs in shared/schedules.ts, but the API adapter also owns a competing definition of that domain rule.

scope.why: The edits stay focused on schedule expected amounts, their consumers, and related tests.

maintainability.why: Competing amount helpers, duplicated tolerance policy, and inconsistent operator propagation leave maintainers multiple definitions to coordinate.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getExpectedScheduleAmount duplicates existing getScheduledAmount dispatch and bypasses getApproxNumberThreshold; scheduleModel.toExternal bypasses the new shared resolver.

disguised_duplication.where: getExpectedScheduleAmount reshapes the existing getScheduledAmount dispatch under a new name, while scheduleModel.toExternal expresses the same resolution decision as a nested ternary.

abstraction_drift.where: The shared resolver gains optional amountOp and an isapprox branch, while scheduleModel.toExternal retains independent resolution and forecast normalization calls the helper without propagating the operator.
